pages.headline: RBI raises bank dividend payout ceiling to 75 per cent
pages.what: The RBI raised the maximum dividend payout ratio to 75 per cent of profit after tax from 40 per cent for eligible commercial, small finance, payments, local area and regional rural banks. Extraordinary income and Level 3 unrealised gains are excluded from PAT.
key: Ceiling: 75 per cent of PAT, earlier 40 per cent
Covers commercial, SFB, payments, local area and regional rural banks
Excluded from PAT: extraordinary income, Level 3 unrealised gains
Overstated profits also excluded
Foreign bank branches remit profits only after audited accounts
pages.static: RBI regulates banks under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; dividend limits are prudential tools linked to capital adequacy.
pages.angle: Trap: reversing the payout numbers or the audit condition.

pages.headline: RBI draft limits customer liability for small frauds
pages.what: The RBI's draft framework would compensate a customer for 85 per cent of net loss or Rs 25,000, whichever is lower, for fraud up to Rs 50,000, once in a lifetime. Banks must pay within five calendar days and may seek reimbursement from the RBI.
key: Applies to fraudulent transactions up to Rs 50,000
Compensation: 85 per cent of net loss or Rs 25,000, whichever is lower
Available once in a lifetime
Banks to pay within five calendar days
Quarterly reimbursement from the RBI; comments by 6 April 2026
pages.static: Customer protection in digital payments flows from RBI circulars on limiting liability of customers in unauthorised transactions.
pages.angle: Trap: swapping 'lower' with 'higher' or dropping the once-in-a-lifetime limit.

pages.headline: Inflation target kept at 4 per cent for 2026-31
pages.what: The Centre retained the flexible inflation target at 4 per cent, with a band of plus or minus 2 per cent, for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031. This is the second extension since 2021. Average inflation was 4.9 per cent after flexible inflation targeting against 6.8 per cent before.
key: Target: 4 per cent CPI inflation, band 2 to 6 per cent
Period: 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031
Statutory basis: Section 45ZA, RBI Act, 1934
Framework adopted in 2016; recommended by Urjit Patel committee
MPC has six members; failure if outside band three straight quarters
pages.static: The Monetary Policy Committee fixes the repo rate to meet the target; the Governor chairs it.
pages.angle: Trap: assuming the RBI alone fixes the target.
pages.remember: Centre sets the target; RBI delivers it.

pages.headline: Rs 1 lakh crore Economic Stabilisation Fund announced
pages.what: With the second Supplementary Demands for 2025-26, the Finance Minister introduced a Rs 1 lakh crore Economic Stabilisation Fund to buffer global shocks. The net cash outgo of the supplementary demands was Rs 57,381.84 crore. The 4.4 per cent fiscal deficit target stays.
key: Fund size: Rs 1 lakh crore
Purpose: fiscal buffer against global shocks
Managed under DEA reserve funds
Net cash outgo from supplementary demands: Rs 57,381.84 crore
Revised 2025-26 fiscal deficit target of 4.4 per cent of GDP unchanged
pages.static: Contingency Fund of India (Article 267) and Consolidated Fund (Article 266) are the main Union funds; supplementary grants need Article 115.
pages.angle: Trap: claiming the Fund raised the deficit target.

pages.headline: 16th Finance Commission keeps States' share at 41 per cent
pages.what: The Sixteenth Finance Commission retained the States' share at 41 per cent for 2026-31, added a GSDP-based 'contribution' criterion and discontinued revenue-deficit grants. It proposed about Rs 3.56 lakh crore for urban local bodies over the period.
key: States' share in divisible pool kept at 41 per cent
Fourteenth Commission raised the share from 32 to 42 per cent
New 'contribution' criterion based on share of GSDP
Revenue-deficit grants discontinued
About Rs 3.56 lakh crore for urban local bodies, 2026-31
pages.static: Article 280 requires a Finance Commission every five years; the Sixteenth is chaired by Arvind Panagariya, and cesses and surcharges are not shareable with States.
pages.angle: Trap: thinking revenue-deficit grants continue.
pages.remember: 41 per cent held; contribution added; revenue-deficit grants gone.

pages.headline: Q3 current account deficit at 1.3 per cent of GDP
pages.what: India's current account deficit for the third quarter of 2025-26 was USD 13.2 billion, 1.3 per cent of GDP, against USD 11.3 billion a year earlier. Reserves fell by USD 24.4 billion. IIP growth was 5.3 per cent.
key: Q3 CAD: USD 13.2 billion (1.3 per cent of GDP)
Year-earlier CAD: USD 11.3 billion (1.1 per cent)
Q2 2025-26 CAD: USD 14.1 billion (1.5 per cent)
Reserves fell USD 24.4 billion in Q3
IIP Q3 growth 5.3 per cent; manufacturing 6.3 per cent
pages.static: The current account records trade, services, income and transfers; the capital account and reserves complete the balance of payments.
pages.angle: Trap: saying reserves rose when the CAD widened.

pages.headline: BHAVYA to build 100 plug-and-play industrial parks
pages.what: The Cabinet approved a central sector scheme, BHAVYA, with Rs 33,660 crore to build 100 investment-ready plug-and-play industrial parks over six years. Projects are chosen in challenge mode, with central support up to Rs 1 crore per acre.
key: Outlay: Rs 33,660 crore, FY2026-27 to FY2031-32
100 plug-and-play industrial parks
Support: Rs 1 crore per acre plus 25 per cent of connectivity cost
Selection through challenge mode
Minimum area 100 acres (25 acres in NE and hilly areas)
pages.static: Industrial corridors and parks fall under the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme, run by DPIIT.
pages.angle: Trap: replacing challenge mode with nomination.

pages.headline: FDI curbs on land-border countries eased
pages.what: DPIIT's Press Note 2 (2026) dropped the rule that the beneficial owner must not be located in a land-border country and adopted the PMLA definition, which uses a threshold above 10 per cent. Pakistan remains subject to government approval and sector bars.
key: Issued by DPIIT on 15 March 2026
Eases Press Note 3 of 2020
Beneficial ownership follows PMLA definition (above 10 per cent)
Pakistan: approval still needed; defence and atomic energy barred
Cabinet decision preceded notification
pages.static: FDI policy is framed by DPIIT under FEMA, 1999; Press Note 3 (2020) required government approval for LBC investment.
pages.angle: Trap: assuming Pakistan was also freed.
pages.remember: Ten per cent test; Pakistan excluded.

pages.headline: RoDTEP cap removed to help exporters
pages.what: The Government fully restored RoDTEP benefits by removing the 50 per cent cap on remission rates introduced in February 2026, citing logistics disruption from the West Asia conflict. RoDTEP covers over 8,500 tariff lines.
key: 50 per cent remission cap (Feb 2026) removed on 23 March
Reason: West Asia conflict disrupting logistics
RoDTEP launched 2021, replacing MEIS
Covers over 8,500 tariff lines
Rebates of 0.5 to 4.3 per cent of FOB value
pages.static: RoDTEP refunds embedded central, State and local taxes not refunded elsewhere, keeping exports WTO-compliant.
pages.angle: Trap: treating a true background fact as the explanation.

pages.headline: RELIEF credit-insurance scheme for exporters
pages.what: The Commerce Ministry launched RELIEF with Rs 497 crore to give credit-insurance cover to exporters affected by the West Asia crisis. New ECGC cover applies from 16 March to 15 June 2026 for exports to 10 West Asian countries.
key: Outlay: Rs 497 crore
Full form: Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation
Insurance by ECGC from 16 March to 15 June 2026
Covers exports to 10 West Asian countries
Up to Rs 50 lakh cover per MSME exporter without prior insurance
pages.static: ECGC (Export Credit Guarantee Corporation) is a Government of India enterprise offering export credit insurance.
pages.angle: Trap: subsidy or cash-grant options in place of insurance.

pages.headline: Critical-mineral auction premium waived in some blocks
pages.what: New rules remove the auction premium on critical minerals that make up less than 10 per cent of block value, except graphite, phosphate and potash. States must decide on mineral-inclusion applications within 60 days. Draft exchange rules name the Indian Bureau of Mines as regulator.
key: Notified 30 March 2026
No auction premium on critical minerals below 10 per cent of block value
Exceptions: graphite, phosphate, potash
60-day deadline for States on inclusion applications
Draft Mineral Exchange Rules (19 March): Indian Bureau of Mines as regulator
pages.static: The MMDR Act, 1957 governs mining; auctions follow the Mineral (Auction) Rules, 2015.
pages.angle: Trap: naming the GSI as regulator.
pages.remember: IBM would run exchanges, not GSI.

pages.headline: Micron's Sanand ATMP plant begins chip production
pages.what: The Prime Minister inaugurated India's first semiconductor Assembly, Test, Marking and Packaging facility, run by Micron Technology at Sanand, Gujarat. It has begun India's first commercial chip production and supports a trusted, self-reliant semiconductor ecosystem.
key: India's first semiconductor ATMP facility
Operator: Micron Technology, at Sanand, Gujarat
First commercial semiconductor chip production in India
ATMP: Assembly, Test, Marking and Packaging
Back-end stage, not wafer fabrication
pages.static: The India Semiconductor Mission, approved in December 2021 with an outlay of Rs 76,000 crore, sits under the Ministry of Electronics and IT.
pages.angle: Trap: confusing packaging with fabrication.
pages.remember: Sanand: first ATMP plant, back-end chips.

pages.headline: Modified UDAN approved with Rs 28,840 crore
pages.what: The Cabinet approved Modified UDAN for FY2026-27 to FY2035-36 with Rs 28,840 crore. It includes 100 new airports from unserved airstrips and 200 helipads, VGF of Rs 10,043 crore and two HAL Dhruv helicopters for Pawan Hans.
key: Outlay: Rs 28,840 crore over ten years
100 new airports and 200 helipads
VGF: Rs 10,043 crore
100 airports get Rs 12,159 crore over eight years
O&M support capped at Rs 3.06 crore per airport per year for three years
pages.static: UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik) began in 2016 under the National Civil Aviation Policy to connect regional airports.
pages.angle: Trap: shifting decimal in the O&M cap.

pages.headline: Small Hydro Power scheme gets Rs 2,585 crore
pages.what: The Cabinet approved a scheme for about 1,500 MW of small hydro projects of 1 to 25 MW. Central assistance is 30 per cent (cap Rs 30 crore) in the North-East and border districts and 20 per cent (cap Rs 20 crore) elsewhere. Only indigenous equipment is allowed.
key: Period: FY2026-27 to FY2030-31; outlay about Rs 2,585 crore
Target: about 1,500 MW from 1-25 MW projects
North-East and border districts: 30 per cent, up to Rs 30 crore
Elsewhere: 20 per cent, up to Rs 20 crore
Indigenous equipment only; about Rs 15,000 crore investment expected
pages.static: Small hydro (up to 25 MW) is administered by MNRE, whereas large hydro is under the Ministry of Power.
pages.angle: Trap: wrong capacity range or imported equipment.
pages.remember: Small hydro: up to 25 MW, made in India.

pages.headline: ECA invoked to protect household LPG
pages.what: India used the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 to direct refiners to maximise LPG output and give households priority over industry and petrochemicals. India imports about 60 per cent of its LPG, so supply disruption in West Asia hit hard.
key: Law: Essential Commodities Act, 1955
Refiners told to maximise LPG production
Households ahead of industry and petrochemicals
India imports about 60 per cent of LPG demand
2020 amendment: foodstuff controls only in extraordinary circumstances
pages.static: The ECA is a statutory tool for price and supply control; the 2020 amendment aimed to liberalise agricultural trade.
pages.angle: Trap: treating the 2020 liberalisation as permanent.

pages.headline: Fuel duties adjusted as Brent crosses USD 111
pages.what: The Centre cut the Special Additional Excise Duty on petrol and diesel and raised export duties on diesel and ATF to reduce under-recoveries of IOCL, BPCL and HPCL. Brent crude was above USD 111 a barrel after Gulf flows through Hormuz were disrupted.
key: SAED on petrol and diesel cut
Export duties on diesel and ATF raised
Beneficiaries: IOCL, BPCL, HPCL
Brent above USD 111 a barrel
Cause: US-Israel conflict with Iran disrupting Hormuz
pages.static: Under-recovery means selling fuel below the cost-linked price; excise duties are levied under the Central Excise Act, 1944.
pages.angle: Trap: believing duty changes raised domestic fuel prices.
pages.remember: Export duty keeps fuel at home.

pages.headline: PM E-DRIVE subsidy periods extended
pages.what: Heavy Industries revised PM E-DRIVE: electric two-wheeler subsidies run to 31 July 2026 and electric three-wheelers (rickshaws and carts) to 31 March 2028. The scheme has a Rs 10,900 crore outlay and plans 72,300 public fast chargers.
key: E-2W subsidy till 31 July 2026
E-3W (rickshaws, carts) till 31 March 2028
Outlay Rs 10,900 crore, approved October 2024
Plan: 72,300 public fast chargers
BHEL to build an EV Super App
pages.static: PM E-DRIVE succeeded the FAME-II scheme to promote electric mobility.
pages.angle: Trap: naming the wrong ministry.

pages.headline: ALMM List-III covers solar ingots and wafers
pages.what: MNRE introduced List-III of the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers for solar ingots and wafers, effective 1 June 2028. It follows the earlier ALMM lists for solar modules and cells and deepens domestic sourcing of the solar supply chain.
key: Issued by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
List-III covers solar ingots and wafers
Effective from 1 June 2028
Follows ALMM lists for modules and cells
Aim: domestic sourcing up the solar value chain
pages.static: ALMM lists aim to ensure that government-linked solar projects use enlisted domestic manufacturers.
pages.angle: Trap: crediting the Ministry of Power.
pages.remember: ALMM List-III: ingots and wafers, 2028, MNRE.

pages.headline: MCGS-MSME widened to service MSMEs
pages.what: The NCGTC guarantees 60 per cent of MSME loans up to Rs 100 crore under MCGS-MSME. The changes allow service-sector MSMEs and cut the minimum machinery-and-equipment share of project cost to 60 per cent from 75 per cent.
key: NCGTC guarantee of 60 per cent
Loans up to Rs 100 crore
Machinery share: 75 per cent to 60 per cent of project cost
Service-sector MSMEs now eligible
Guarantee lasts 10 years; ceiling of Rs 7 lakh crore of guarantees
pages.static: NCGTC is a company owned by the Department of Financial Services; credit guarantee reduces collateral demands on MSMEs.
pages.angle: Trap: reversing eligibility (manufacturing only).

pages.headline: Banks told to use Grameen Credit Score
pages.what: The Department of Financial Services made the Grameen Credit Score the default tool to assess rural borrowers, mainly first-time ones. The 300-900 score is developed by credit information companies using data from Kisan Credit Cards, SVAMITVA, priority sector loans and tractor loans.
key: Scale: 300 to 900
Developed by credit information companies
Phase I data: KCC, SVAMITVA, priority sector loans, tractor loans
Announced in Union Budget 2025-26
Issued as a direction by the Department of Financial Services
pages.static: Credit information companies are regulated under the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005.
pages.angle: Trap: assuming a different scale or the RBI as author.

pages.headline: Panel suggests IPOs for profitable RRBs
pages.what: A Parliamentary panel recommended stock-market listing for profitable Regional Rural Banks. RRBs earned Rs 7,720 crore in the first nine months of FY2025-26, and gross NPAs fell to 5.4 per cent. Amalgamation under One State-One RRB cut their number from 196 to 28.
key: IPOs recommended for profitable RRBs
Net profit Rs 7,720 crore (first nine months FY2025-26)
Gross NPA 5.4 per cent, a 13-year low
One State-One RRB: 196 to 28
Ownership: Centre 50, sponsor bank 35, State 15
pages.static: RRBs were set up under the RRB Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Narasimham Working Group.
pages.angle: Trap: privatisation versus listing.

pages.headline: SEBI adopts insider norms for its own top officials
pages.what: The SEBI Board accepted its High-Level Committee's report treating the Chairman and Whole-Time Members as insiders. Equity holdings must be liquidated, frozen or sold on joining, and investment in any one intermediary's products is capped at 25 per cent of the portfolio.
key: Chairman and Whole-Time Members treated as insiders
Equity holdings to be liquidated, frozen or sold on joining
Cap: 25 per cent of financial portfolio in one intermediary's products
Limits extend to spouses and dependents prospectively
Initial, annual and event-based disclosures
pages.static: SEBI was set up under the SEBI Act, 1992 to regulate securities markets.
pages.angle: Trap: reading the rules as a ban on all investments.

pages.headline: New GDP series with base year 2022-23
pages.when: Reported in March 2026 (release date not given in sources)
pages.what: MoSPI released new annual and quarterly national accounts with 2022-23 as the base year. Double deflation is used in manufacturing and agriculture, and GST, e-Vahan and PFMS data are integrated. GDP at current prices is about 3 to 4 per cent smaller.
key: Base year 2022-23 replaces 2011-12
Released by MoSPI
Double deflation replaces single deflation
New sources: GST, e-Vahan, PFMS
Current-price GDP about 3-4 per cent smaller (Shankar IAS)
pages.static: National accounts follow the UN System of National Accounts; the NSO under MoSPI compiles them.
pages.angle: Trap: attributing release to NITI Aayog or the RBI.

pages.headline: ASUSE 2025 results released
pages.what: MoSPI's National Statistical Office released the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises for January to December 2025. It covers non-agricultural unincorporated firms in manufacturing, trade and services and feeds GDP estimates.
key: Conducted by the National Statistical Office, MoSPI
Period: January to December 2025
Covers unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises
Sectors: manufacturing, trade, services
Indicators: employment, GVA, wages, digital usage
pages.static: The Annual Survey of Industries, by contrast, covers registered factories.
pages.angle: Trap: assuming agriculture is covered.

pages.headline: Core industries growth slows to 2.3 per cent in February
pages.what: The combined index of the eight core industries grew 2.3 per cent in February 2026, down from 4.7 per cent in January. The eight industries make up 40.27 per cent of the weight of the Index of Industrial Production and the index is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT.
key: February 2026 growth: 2.3 per cent (January 4.7 per cent)
Eight: coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilizers, steel, cement, electricity
Weight in IIP: 40.27 per cent
Released by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
Iron ore not in the list
pages.static: The IIP is compiled by the NSO under MoSPI; the core index is a leading indicator of it.
pages.angle: 'NOT' questions: iron ore or sugar are classic traps.
pages.remember: Coal, oil, gas, refinery, fertilizer, steel, cement, power.
